description:
Two variants of polynomial interpolation on `FieldPoly<F>`.

## API

- `pub fn interpolate(points: &[(F, F)]) -> Result<FieldPoly<F>, InterpolationError>` — standard Lagrange, O(n²). Returns zero polynomial for empty input. `InterpolationError::DuplicatePoint` if any two `x_i` coincide.
- `pub fn interpolate_fast(points: &[(F, F)]) -> Result<FieldPoly<F>, InterpolationError>` — subproduct-tree-based O(n log² n): build `M(x) = Π(x − x_i)`, compute `M'(x)`, evaluate `M'` at all `x_i` via `batch_evaluate`, then one downward pass.
- Both routines must reuse `batch_ops::batch_inverse` for the `1 / Π_{j!=i}(x_i − x_j)` weights — cite this dependency explicitly in the module docs (this was the motivating application for the Montgomery-trick dep).
- Threshold constant selecting naive vs fast, tuned by a bench case.

## Success criteria

- Round-trip proptest: `interpolate(points).evaluate(x_i) == y_i` for all points (verbatim from story spec).
- Agreement proptest: `interpolate_fast` matches `interpolate` for `n` up to 32.
- Unit tests: duplicate x detection, empty input, single-point.
- Bench table in module doc showing fast path beating naive at the threshold crossover.
- `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -- -D warnings`/`cargo test --release` clean.
